changedEntries.text: Pattern mission. What comes next?
The rook moves along a row or column. It cannot pass through a piece. Move the rook along its clear row to the star square.
The rook moves along a row or column. It cannot pass through a piece. Move the rook straight up to the star square.
The bishop moves diagonally. It cannot pass through a piece. Move the bishop along the clear diagonal.
The knight moves in an L shape and can jump over pieces. Move the knight in its L-shape to the star square.
The king moves one square in any direction. Move the king one square to the star.
The queen moves along rows, columns or diagonals. It cannot pass through a piece. Move the queen straight up the clear file.
The knight moves in an L shape and can jump over pieces. Jump the knight in an L-shape over the blocker.
The rook moves along a row or column. It cannot pass through a piece. Move the rook left along the clear row.
The bishop moves diagonally. It cannot pass through a piece. Move the bishop along a clear diagonal.
The king moves one square in any direction. Move the king one square down.

The rook moves along a row or column. It cannot pass through a piece. Capture the marked pawn only if its square is safe. Capture the marked pawn with the rook, then check that its landing square is safe.
The knight moves in an L shape and can jump over pieces. Capture the marked pawn only if its square is safe. Capture the marked pawn with the knight safely.
The bishop moves diagonally. It cannot pass through a piece. Capture the marked pawn only if its square is safe. Capture the marked pawn along the diagonal, if it is safe.
The queen moves along rows, columns or diagonals. It cannot pass through a piece. Capture the marked pawn only if its square is safe. Capture the marked pawn with the queen safely.
The rook moves along a row or column. It cannot pass through a piece. Capture the marked pawn only if its square is safe. Capture the marked pawn along the row safely.
The bishop moves diagonally. It cannot pass through a piece. Capture the marked pawn only if its square is safe. Capture the marked pawn along the diagonal safely.
The rook moves along a row or column. It cannot pass through a piece. Capture the marked pawn only if its square is safe. Capture the marked pawn up the file safely.
The rook moves along a row or column. It cannot pass through a piece. Move along the clear row to the goal; a pawn blocks the rook’s upward path.
The bishop moves diagonally. It cannot pass through a piece. Slide the bishop diagonally to the goal.
The knight moves in an L shape and can jump over pieces. The knight jumps over pieces to land on the star.
The king moves one square in any direction. Move the king one square diagonally to the goal.
The queen moves along rows, columns or diagonals. It cannot pass through a piece. Use the queen’s diagonal path to reach the goal.
The rook moves along a row or column. It cannot pass through a piece. Move across the clear row to the goal; leave the friendly pawn alone.
The knight moves in an L shape and can jump over pieces. Jump in an L-shape to reach the goal.
The bishop moves diagonally. It cannot pass through a piece. Move diagonally to the marked square.
The queen moves along rows, columns or diagonals. It cannot pass through a piece. Move straight down the open file.
The king moves one square in any direction. Move the king one square up to the goal.
Mission clue. Think about the brightest thing we see in daytime and how it warms the ground.
Mission clue. The Moon travels near one of these objects. Which choice is the planet where we live?
Mission clue. The nickname comes from the rusty colour of its dusty ground. Which planet in the choices fits?
Mission clue. Astronauts have a special name for the clothing they wear outside a spacecraft.
Mission clue. Spacecraft need power for many systems. Look at how sunlight is collected.
Mission clue. Compare a rover with a flying robot: which one explores the surface?
Mission clue. Look at where the Moon is in relation to the Sun and Earth.
Mission clue. Most of Earth’s surface is ocean. Think about what oceans are made of.
Mission clue. What information could help scientists plan a rover’s next move?
Mission clue. Earth from space has no corners. Which shape choice fits a world like that?
Mission clue. At launch, watch the direction the rocket rises and the direction its exhaust travels.
Mission clue. Think about the layer a spacecraft travels through before reaching space.
Mission clue. What do you notice when a ball falls after you let it go?
Mission clue. Use a globe and lamp to explore which side is lit as the globe moves.
Mission clue. Think about how water can stay frozen in cold places, including places hidden from view.
Mission clue. A spacecraft becomes very hot as it enters a planet’s air. What could help it survive?
Mission clue. Watch what happens when a falling leaf spreads out and catches air.
Mission clue. Look at the rover’s communication equipment, not the parts that touch the ground.
Mission clue. Think about how sunlight reaches different parts of Earth during the year.
Mission clue. The names are Phobos and Deimos. Count the names.
Mission clue. Before crossing a rocky patch, what information would help a rover choose a safe direction?
Mission clue. Imagine a lander touching down on rough ground. What could stop it wobbling?
Mission clue. Imagine tracing a curved route around a star or planet. Which choice names that kind of route?
Mission clue. Think about the long distance between Earth and Mars when a command is sent.
Mission clue. The choices have very different air and surface temperatures. Which one has the thickest, hottest air?
Mission clue. One choice is a giant planet, while the other two are rocky worlds. Which is the largest?
Mission clue. The question is about an icy moon, not a planet. Which moon fits the description?
Mission clue. Think about what changes when a parachute has a wider canopy.
Mission clue. Compare power sources used by spacecraft in places with little sunlight.
Mission clue. Think about the great distance a radio message must cross between Earth and Mars.
Mission clue. One of these planets is easy to recognize by the bright bands around it.
Mission clue. Mars teams use a special word when planning a rover’s daily schedule.
Mission clue. A rover collects small pieces for scientists to study later. What could keep one safe?
Mission clue. Compare the power sources spacecraft can use when they travel close to the Sun.
Mission clue. Compare the arrows showing how Venus and most planets turn.
Mission clue. Look at the ground around a rover and decide what information a route planner needs.
